proof:
Source: step 4 (parent C2) of the parent proof (the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dt_cube_bv_median: the least integer β with Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β}) ≥ 1/2 is a median; (a) a median minimizes c ↦ ∫_{Q₁}|u − c|; (b) |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|). In Simon these are the integer median choice (31) and the bound (35) in the proof of Ch. 6, 5.1 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1879–1883 and 1906–1908), whose minimizing property replaces the median hypothesis 2.7(‡) of Ch. 2.

Notation (used throughout). m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1 ≥ 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate and e_1, …, e_n is the standard orthonormal basis. Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} (so Q_0 = Q₁). div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv ℝ G x, viewed as a linear map). For v : ℝⁿ → ℝ, ‖Dv(x)‖ is the operator norm of fderiv ℝ v x, which equals the Euclidean length |∇v(x)| of the gradient. Integrals over a set are Bochner integrals for the restricted Lebesgue measure. Under the measure-preserving, coordinate-preserving continuous linear equivalence WithLp.ofLp : Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp / EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp; it is not an isometry for the sup norm of Fin n → ℝ, and no isometry property is used) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ); hence vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded, and Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁ for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Let u be integer-valued and integrable on Q₁. Write μ for Lebesgue measure restricted to Q₁; μ(ℝⁿ) = vol(Q₁) = 1, and μ{P} denotes μ{y : P(y)}.

0. Measurability. u is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ, so there is a Borel function u' with u = u' μ-a.e.; hence each set {u ≤ c}, {u < c}, {u ≥ c}, {u > c} is μ-null-measurable and has the same μ-measure as the corresponding set for u' (equivalently, replace u' by the integer-valued Borel function round ∘ u', which equals u μ-a.e. because round(u(y)) = u(y)). All quantities in the statement (∫_{Q₁}|u − β|, ∫_{Q₁}|u − c|, ∫_{Q₁}|u|) are integrals of μ-integrable functions (μ is finite and u is μ-integrable), and they are unchanged under μ-a.e. modification; the pointwise inequalities below hold μ-a.e.

1. Distribution function. F(c) := μ{u ≤ c} is nondecreasing in c. As k → ∞ through ℕ, {u ≤ k} increases to ℝⁿ (u is real-valued), so F(k) → μ(ℝⁿ) = 1 by continuity from below; and {u ≤ −k} decreases to ∅, so F(−k) → 0 by continuity from above (μ is finite). Hence S := {k ∈ ℤ : F(k) ≥ 1/2} is nonempty (it contains large k) and bounded below (choose K with F(−K) < 1/2; then F(k) ≤ F(−K) < 1/2 for every integer k ≤ −K, so S ⊆ (−K, ∞)). Let β := min S (Mathlib Int.exists_least_of_bdd).

2. Median properties. F(β) = μ{u ≤ β} ≥ 1/2 and F(β − 1) < 1/2. Since u is integer-valued, {u > β − 1} = {u ≥ β}, so μ{u ≥ β} = 1 − F(β − 1) > 1/2. Consequently μ{u > β} = 1 − μ{u ≤ β} ≤ 1/2 and μ{u < β} = 1 − μ{u ≥ β} < 1/2.

3. Minimality: ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ ∫_{Q₁}|u − c| for every c ∈ ℝ.
 Case c ≥ β. Pointwise, on {u ≤ β} we have u ≤ β ≤ c, so |u − c| − |u − β| = (c − u) − (β − u) = c − β; on {u > β}, |u − c| − |u − β| ≥ −|c − β| = −(c − β) by the triangle inequality. Integrating over Q₁: ∫|u − c| − ∫|u − β| ≥ (c − β)(μ{u ≤ β} − μ{u > β}) ≥ (c − β)(1/2 − 1/2) = 0.
 Case c < β. On {u ≥ β}, |u − c| − |u − β| = (u − c) − (u − β) = β − c; on {u < β}, |u − c| − |u − β| ≥ −(β − c). Integrating: ∫|u − c| − ∫|u − β| ≥ (β − c)(μ{u ≥ β} − μ{u < β}) ≥ (β − c)(1/2 − 1/2) = 0.

4. Size of β. If β > 0: on {u ≥ β}, |u| ≥ u ≥ β, so ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ βμ{u ≥ β} ≥ β/2. If β < 0: on {u ≤ β}, |u| ≥ −u ≥ −β = |β|, so ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ |β|μ{u ≤ β} ≥ |β|/2. If β = 0 the claim is trivial since ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ 0. Hence |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|. ∎
key_steps: Work μ-a.e. with a Borel representative (u = u' a.e., round ∘ u' integer-valued); vol(Q₁) = 1.
β := least integer k with vol(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ k}) ≥ 1/2 exists by continuity of the distribution function from below and above.
Integer values give vol{u ≥ β} > 1/2 and vol{u ≤ β} ≥ 1/2, so β is a median.
A median minimizes c ↦ ∫_{Q₁}|u − c| (pointwise comparison on {u ≤ β}, {u > β}, respectively {u ≥ β}, {u < β}).
|u| ≥ |β| on a set of measure ≥ 1/2, so |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.
